context_documents.title: 2023-3005 · Separate contact development can outperform one compromised gripper
context_documents.body:
# 2023-3005: Separate contact development can outperform one compromised gripper

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A telescoping arm on a braced A-frame uses a highly articulated wrist and distinct cone/cube contact arrangements. The interview reports eleven cone-intake iterations versus four cube-intake generations.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team’s stated goal is a light, fast robot that acquires cones in different orientations and scores high/mid; the different contact systems emerged through tests.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The separate iteration counts show that the two pieces presented different problems. Avoid inferring that a more complex-looking gripper was unnecessary without comparing acquisition and release reliability. Bracing saves upper structural mass only if its tension and anchors remain repeatable.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test both pieces, cable-brace tension and wrist motion limits; include calibration and replacement time.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: 3005 RoboChargers CAD release
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the team-authored posts and technical replies at these locators.
source_reviews.facts: Team says arm gearbox pivots by slip fit around tower cross tube and is axially retained by collars. Two turnbuckles tension the chain. Team cites shaft parallelism, tracking adjustment, simpler parts and a crossmember already needed for support. Most prints PLA/PLA+, with selected Onyx such as telescope e-chain support.
source_reviews.limitations: Team warns the working CAD snapshot contains broken elements and differences from the robot. Model not measured.

source_reviews.title: 3005 interview
source_reviews.review_basis: Inherited synopsis. No fresh full-caption or visual review.
source_reviews.facts: Older interview describes a telescoping pivot arm on a braced A-frame, articulated direct wrist and separate cone and cube contact geometry.
source_reviews.limitations: Treat specific details and configuration dates as provisional.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: AMP uses a pivoting telescope to position a wrist that can handle both game pieces. The team CAD discussion gives an unusually clear account of how its arm transmission fits into the tower. The gearbox rotates around a cross tube the team already needed structurally, and turnbuckles adjust the chain. This makes the tower tube part of both the structure and the transmission alignment scheme.
piece_flow: Set the wrist for the intended piece. The older interview reports separate cone and cube contact geometries, including pickup of upright and tipped pieces.
Capture directly and retain while the arm pivots and telescopes. There is no intermediate transfer in the older account.
Set wrist angle for the node and release. Retract so the wrist and its harness clear the bumper and tower.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Putting the arm transmission on a structural tube saves a separate adjustment slide. Pivoting the gearbox ideally preserves shaft parallelism during tensioning, but only if the support tube is straight and its relation to the arm shaft survives loading. The telescope also moves the e-chain and tool together. The team identified its e-chain support as one of the few places where it used an Onyx print.

subsystems.name: Pivot-adjusted chain transmission
subsystems.construction: Team describes slip-fit gearbox plates around an aluminum cross tube, collars and two tensioning turnbuckles.
subsystems.operation: Pivot the gearbox to adjust chain center distance. Set lateral tracking before securing it axially.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team wanted a low-part-count adjustment that kept shafts parallel and reused a structural member.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The mount has to react chain load and motor torque after adjustment. A small increase in play can change chain tracking or tension during fast arm reversals.
subsystems.interfaces: Cross tube, gearbox plates, turnbuckles and arm sprocket share the force path.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Mark collar and turnbuckle positions and measure chain tension through an arm cycle. Check for movement after an abrupt reversal.
subsystems.unknowns: Mount fit, allowable deflection and adjustment torque.

subsystems.name: Telescoping arm and e-chain
subsystems.construction: Older account describes braced A-frame and cable bracing. Team identifies an Onyx print supporting telescope e-chain.
subsystems.operation: The arm swings to establish elevation and extends to reach the node while the carrier manages wiring.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older interview synopsis attributes selection over a slanted elevator to expected mass and speed advantages.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A lightweight distal arm can accelerate faster, but its deflection and wiring drag may dominate final tool placement.
subsystems.interfaces: Pivot angle, telescope stroke and wrist articulation determine reach, harness curvature and loaded center of mass.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Run the full stroke at both pivot extremes and check chain support for binding or cracks after repeated reversals.
subsystems.unknowns: Actual arm mass, print loading and extension drive details.

subsystems.name: Dual-piece wrist
subsystems.construction: Separate contacts and articulated wrist are described in the older interview.
subsystems.operation: Configure the tool for the piece and retain it from supply through release.
subsystems.team_rationale: The older account describes extensive prototype iteration separately for cone and cube pickup.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Separate contact zones allow tuning, but the idle side must clear the other piece and adjacent nodes.
subsystems.interfaces: Wrist pose determines what enters the tool and where it is released relative to the arm axis.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test an upright cone, tipped cone and off-center cube in repeated loaded cycles. Measure release scatter, not only capture success.
subsystems.unknowns: Final contact geometry, actuator count and sensing.

revisions: CAD release is an April working snapshot. Reported cone and cube generation numbers from the older account are prototype counts, not fielded versions.
transferable_principles: Reuse a structural pivot for adjustment when it also provides shaft alignment and can carry the complete reaction load.
disconfirming_conditions: Use another mount when the structural tube deflects enough to alter tracking, or when chain adjustment requires removing the wrist, harness or bumpers.
remaining_gaps: Full captions, verified as-built geometry, tested load range and station implementation.
recommended_images: Team gearbox photo in post 6 and a source-linked full-stroke view of e-chain and wrist.
